titulo_es: So, such, too y enough (grado y consecuencia)
descripcion_es: Intensificar con so y such, expresar exceso con too y suficiencia con enough; posición y estructuras con that e infinitivo.
resumen: So y such intensifican («tan», «tal») y pueden introducir una consecuencia con that. Too indica exceso («demasiado») y enough, suficiencia («lo bastante»). Cada uno tiene su posición fija.

filas: The film was so boring that I fell asleep.
It was such a boring film that I fell asleep.
too + adjetivo (+ for alguien) (+ to infinitivo)
This coffee is too hot to drink.
He isn't old enough to vote.

items: Such a/an con sustantivo contable singular: such a nice day. Sin artículo con plurales e incontables: such nice people, such bad weather.
So con much, many, few, little: so many people, so much money.
Too tiene sentido negativo (exceso): It's too expensive = no puedo comprarlo. Para «muy» positivo se usa very o so.
Enough va DETRÁS del adjetivo pero DELANTE del sustantivo: warm enough / enough time.

explicacion.texto: No confundas too (demasiado) con too much / too many (demasiado + sustantivo): too much sugar, too many cars. Delante de un adjetivo solo, nunca too much: too tired, no too much tired.

ejemplos.frase: She was so tired that she went to bed at eight.
ejemplos.traduccion: Estaba tan cansada que se acostó a las ocho.

ejemplos.frase: They're such good friends that they went on holiday together.
ejemplos.traduccion: Son tan buenos amigos que se fueron juntos de vacaciones.

ejemplos.frase: The box is too heavy for me to carry.
ejemplos.traduccion: La caja pesa demasiado para que yo la lleve.

ejemplos.frase: Is the room big enough for six people?
ejemplos.traduccion: ¿Es la habitación lo bastante grande para seis personas?

ejemplos.frase: There were so many tourists that we couldn't see the painting.
ejemplos.traduccion: Había tantos turistas que no pudimos ver el cuadro.

ejemplos.frase: I didn't have enough time to finish the exam.
ejemplos.traduccion: No tuve tiempo suficiente para terminar el examen.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: It was a so beautiful day.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: It was such a beautiful day.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Delante de un sustantivo se usa such a, no a so.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: He isn't enough tall to play basketball.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: He isn't tall enough to play basketball.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I'm too much tired to go out.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I'm too tired to go out.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Delante de un adjetivo solo se usa too, sin much.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: This town is too nice, I love it.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: This town is so nice, I love it.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Too implica exceso negativo; para elogiar se usa so o very.

ejercicios.frase: It was ___ cold day that we stayed inside.
The music was ___ loud that I couldn't hear you.
She's ___ young to drive. She's only fifteen.
ejercicios.explicacion: Exceso que impide algo: too + adjetivo + to.
Sustantivo en plural: such sin artículo.

ejercicios.frase: I've never seen ___ much snow in Madrid.
It was ___ bad weather that the flight was cancelled.
ejercicios.explicacion: Weather es incontable: such sin artículo.

ejercicios.frase: The water isn't warm ___ to swim.

ejercicios.enunciado: Completa con too much o too many.
ejercicios.frase: You put ___ salt in the soup.
This jacket is enough big for me.
respuestas: This jacket is big enough for me.
He is such a good cook.
ejercicios.explicacion: Ante sustantivo: such a + adjetivo + sustantivo.

ejercicios.frase: The book was so interesting that I read it in one day.
respuestas: It was such an interesting book that I read it in one day.
ejercicios.explicacion: So + adjetivo pasa a such an + adjetivo + sustantivo (an delante de vocal).

ejercicios.frase: The tea is very hot. I can't drink it.
respuestas: The tea is too hot to drink.
The tea is too hot for me to drink.
ejercicios.explicacion: Too + adjetivo + to infinitivo; no se repite it.

respuestas: she isn't old enough to vote
